questions.question_text: The daily earnings of a taxi driver in a city has an average of 2400 and a standard deviation of 360. If a random sample of 45 taxi drivers are surveyed, the probability of the average daily earnings in the sample being between 2300 and 2500 is:
Shoppers enter the City Mall at an average of 32 per hour. What is the probability at least 13 customers enter the mall in the next 30 minutes? It is:
questions.explanation: Formula: Poisson P(X ≥ k) = 1 - P(X < k). Steps: Rate = 32/hour. For 30 min, λ = 32 × 0.5 = 16. P(X ≥ 13) = 1 - P(X ≤ 12). Using Poisson(λ=16), P(X ≤ 12) ≈ 0.22. So P(X ≥ 13) ≈ 0.78. Result: Between 0.75 and 1.00.

questions.question_text: If A and B are mutually exclusive events with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.5, then P(A u B) is equal to:
questions.explanation: Formula: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B). For mutually exclusive events, P(A ∩ B) = 0. Steps: P(A ∪ B) = 0.3 + 0.5 - 0 = 0.8. Result: 0.8.

questions.question_text: Scores of 12 job applicants in a screening test is as follows: 18, 23, 27, 21, 32, 17, 20, 29, 22, 30, 25, and 15. Determine the first quartile.
Daily demand at a local store can take values of 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 with probabilities 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2, and 0.2 respectively. The standard deviation of daily sales is:
For a given product, the supply (y) and price(x) for 8 weeks is given as (y,x) as: (5, 2), (7, 4), (9, 8), (12, 5), (10, 7), (13, 8), (16, 16) and (16, 6). The sample covariance is equal to:
questions.explanation: Formula: Cov(X,Y) = (1/(n-1)) × Σ(xi - x̄)(yi - ȳ). Steps: Calculate means: x̄ = 7.0, ȳ = 8.125. Compute Σ(xi - x̄)(yi - ȳ) = 79.875. Cov = 79.875/(8-1) = 11.41 ≈ 11.4. Result: 11.4.

questions.question_text: Scores on a national competitive exam were normally distributed with a mean of 80 and a variance of 36. If the top 5% of test scores receive merit awards, what is the lowest score eligible for a merit award? It is:
questions.explanation: Formula: X ~ N(μ, σ²), find x such that P(X > x) = 0.05. Steps: μ = 80, σ = √36 = 6. For top 5%, z = 1.645. x = μ + z×σ = 80 + 1.645×6 = 89.87 ≈ 90. Result: 90.

questions.question_text: John, Mary and Sue at a fast-food restaurant pack the take-out dinners. John packs 45% of the dinners but fails to include a salt packet 4% of the time. Mary packs 25% of the dinners but omits the salt packet 2% of the time. Sue packs 30% of the dinners but fails to include the salt packet 3% of the time. If you have purchased dinner and find that there is no salt packet, what is the probability that Sue packed your dinner?
questions.explanation: Formula: Bayes' theorem P(Sue|No Salt) = P(No Salt|Sue)×P(Sue) / P(No Salt). Steps: P(No Salt) = 0.45×0.04 + 0.25×0.02 + 0.30×0.03 = 0.032. P(Sue|No Salt) = (0.03×0.30)/0.032 = 0.009/0.032 = 0.28125 ≈ 0.28. Result: 0.28.

questions.question_text: It is believed that 70% of the customers at a retail chain are satisfied with their shopping experience. If a random sample of 20 shoppers are surveyed, what is the probability that at least 12 are not satisfied with their shopping experience? It is:
questions.explanation: Formula: Binomial P(X ≥ k) = 1 - P(X ≤ k-1). Steps: n = 20, p = 0.30 (not satisfied), find P(X ≥ 12). P(X ≥ 12) = 1 - P(X ≤ 11). Using Binomial(n=20, p=0.30), P(X ≤ 11) ≈ 0.995. So P(X ≥ 12) ≈ 0.005. Result: Between 0.00 and 0.25.

questions.question_text: The probability that a t-random variable with 5 degrees of freedom takes values between -2.0 and 0.5 is:
questions.explanation: Formula: t-distribution P(-2.0 < t < 0.5) with df = 5. Steps: Using t-table, P(t < 0.5) ≈ 0.68, P(t < -2.0) ≈ 0.05. P(-2.0 < t < 0.5) = 0.68 - 0.05 = 0.63. Result: Between 0.60 and 0.80.

questions.question_text: A department store has determined that 25% of all their sales are credit sales. If a random sample of 60 sales records are selected, the probability of the proportion of credit sales in the sample being more than 30% is:

The time it takes a mechanic to change the oil in a car is exponentially distributed with a mean of 25 minutes. What is the probability that the mechanic takes less than 40 minutes to change oil in a car? It is:
questions.explanation: Formula: Exponential P(X < x) = 1 - e^(-λx) where λ = 1/μ. Steps: Mean μ = 25, so λ = 1/25 = 0.04. P(X < 40) = 1 - e^(-0.04×40) = 1 - e^(-1.6) = 1 - 0.202 ≈ 0.798. Result: Between 0.75 and 1.00.
